meta.purpose: Scientific ecological analysis of each region — soil, climate, mushroom ecology, pollinator habitat, crop suitability, microclimates
sources: Dhouni et al. 2024 - Physicochemical properties of Kumaon hill soils
Pande et al. - Soil Nutrient Evaluation in Almora District
Kumar & Ravi 2025 - Wild mushroom diversity from mid-Himalayas
Burnett et al. 2008 - Slope aspect impacts on soil temperature
Singh 2018 - Aspect impacts in trans-Himalayan valley

soil.type: Red and yellow sandy loam (Kumaon classification)
soil.phSuitability: IDEAL — most crops need 5.5-7.0. This range is perfect.
soil.ec: 0.08-0.31 dSm⁻¹ (low — not saline, good for plants)
soil.depth: Moderate — rocky in places, needs terracing
soil.drainage: Good on slopes, needs management in valley bottoms
soil.amendmentNeeded: Cow dung compost (you'll have plenty), green manure from berseem

microclimate.southFacing: Warmer (+2-3°C), drier, more sun. Better for: tomatoes, peppers, warm-season crops. More evapotranspiration.
microclimate.northFacing: Cooler, moister, more vegetation. Better for: leafy greens, mushrooms, shade-loving plants.
microclimate.ridgeTop: Windy, exposed. Good for: windbreak trees, bee hives (less wind than valley).
microclimate.valleyBottom: Warmer, more humid, flood risk in monsoon. Good for: water-loving crops, rice paddies if irrigated.
microclimate.practicalImpact: On your 5 acres, south-facing slopes = warm-season garden. North-facing = mushroom log placement + shade crops.

mushroomEcology.wildSpecies: 60+ species documented in Kumaon Hills (Kumar & Ravi 2025). Peak fruiting Jul-Nov during monsoon.
mushroomEcology.substrate: Dead logs, leaf litter, hardwood — abundant in pine/deodar forest

cordyceps.note: Needs controlled indoor environment, not outdoor ecology

mushroomEcology.naturalForage: Wild mushrooms fruit Jul-Nov in forests around Almora. Shaggy mane, oyster, and medicinal species documented.
mushroomEcology.verdict: EXCELLENT — altitude, humidity, substrate abundance, and existing wild mushroom diversity all favor cultivation.

pollinators.managedSpecies: Apis mellifera (Italian bee) — suitable for your 2 hives
pollinators.wildSpecies: Apis cerana (Indian hive bee), various bumblebees, butterflies, hoverflies
pollinators.floweringSeason: April-June (peak), with rhododendrons Feb-Apr, wildflowers May-Oct
pollinators.forageQuality: HIGH — Himalayan wildflowers, rhododendrons, apple blossoms, berberis, wild herbs
pollinators.verdict: EXCELLENT — diverse wildflower calendar, long foraging season (Apr-Oct)

apples.notes: 5500-6500ft is prime. Chaubatia Gardens nearby proves it.

turmeric.notes: Needs 280-300 days. Warm enough in summer but marginal at 6500ft. Better at lower elevation sites.

ginger.notes: Grow under trees or shade cloth. Needs consistent moisture.

potatoes.notes: Native crop. Kumaon is potato country.

rajma.notes: Traditional Kumaon crop. Plant in monsoon, harvest Sep-Oct.

leafyGreens.notes: Spinach, mustard greens, kale — grow almost year-round.

ashwagandha.notes: Needs warm soil. Feb-Mar plant, Nov-Dec harvest.

tea.notes: Kausani has tea gardens but Almora is borderline. Possible with irrigation.

soil.type: Deep rich forest soil (proven by orange orchards)
soil.texture: Sandy loam to loam, deep profile
soil.ph: 5.5-6.5 (estimated — same belt as Almora but deeper soil)
soil.cec: Good to very good (orange orchards prove sustained fertility)
soil.organicCarbon: High — deep forest soil with leaf litter accumulation
soil.depth: DEEP — best of all options. Orange roots need deep soil.
soil.erosionRisk: Low — gentle slopes, good vegetation cover
soil.verdict: BEST SOIL of all regions. Deep, fertile, proven by decades of orange production.

microclimate.southFacing: Warmer, drier. Orange orchards typically on south-facing slopes for sun.
microclimate.northFacing: Cooler, moister. Good for shade crops, mushroom logs.
microclimate.valleyFloor: Warmer, more humid. Good for vegetables.
microclimate.note: Rolling terrain = more aspect variety = more microclimates = more crop niches.

mushroomEcology.wildSpecies: Similar to Almora — same altitude band. Monsoon fruiting Jul-Nov.
mushroomEcology.substrate: Orange orchards provide pruned wood — free substrate for shiitake logs
mushroomEcology.verdict: GOOD — orange orchards provide pruning waste as mushroom substrate. Seasonal, not year-round outdoor.

pollinators.forageQuality: EXCELLENT — orange blossoms (spring) + wildflowers + forest herbs
pollinators.orangeBlossoms: Major spring forage — Feb-Apr. Strong nectar flow.
pollinators.verdict: EXCELLENT — orange orchards = best bee forage of any region

oranges.notes: PROVEN — orange orchards are the signature. Climate and soil perfect.

lychee.notes: Possible at this altitude with warm microclimate.

soil.texture: Sandy loam, shallow to moderately shallow
soil.cec: Low to moderate — needs significant amendment
soil.depth: SHALLOW — major limitation for root crops
soil.drainage: Excellent — ridge drains fast (too fast for some crops)
soil.amendmentNeeded: Heavy composting needed. Lime to raise pH. Green manure crops.
soil.verdict: WEAKEST SOIL — shallow, acidic, needs work. But tea gardens prove it CAN support crops with management.

microclimate.ridgeTop: Most of Kausani is ridge. Wind-exposed, fast-draining. Good airflow for mushroom logs.
microclimate.southSlope: Warmer, drier. Better for warm-season crops.
microclimate.northSlope: Cooler, moister. Better for cool-season crops.
microclimate.note: Narrow ridge = limited flat land but dramatic microclimate diversity within short distances.

mushroomEcology.verdict: GOOD — ridge position provides excellent air circulation for mushroom logs. Pine forest provides substrate. But shallow soil limits outdoor cultivation beds.

pollinators.forageQuality: GOOD — wildflowers, forest herbs, tea garden blooms
pollinators.verdict: GOOD — not as rich as Peora's orange blossoms but sufficient.

tea.notes: PROVEN — Kausani tea gardens exist. Ridge position + rainfall = ideal for tea.

potatoes.notes: Shallow soil limits yield. Better for above-ground crops.

leafyGreens.notes: Cool climate suits them. Shallow soil is less of an issue for shallow-rooted greens.

soil.texture: Silty loam to loam, dark brown
soil.depth: THIN — steep slopes prevent deep soil accumulation
soil.verdict: WEAKEST FOR FARMING — thin soil on steep slopes. Better left as forest.

microclimate.note: At 7400ft, significantly colder than other options. South-facing slopes still receive good sun but steepness limits cultivation.
microclimate.snowCover: Dec-Feb, regular snowfall. Shortens growing season to 7 months.

mushroomEcology.verdict: POOR for outdoor — thin soil, steep slopes. INDOOR lab possible but power access limited (no borewell).

apples.notes: 7400ft = prime apple zone. Tehri Garhwal is apple country.

mostCrops.notes: Too steep, too cold, thin soil. Only apples and hardy root crops viable.

soil.type: Alluvial valley floor, metamorphic on slopes
soil.fertility: Medium — river alluvium fertile but limited area
soil.depth: Valley floor: deep. Slopes: very thin.
soil.drainage: Valley: can waterlog. Slopes: too fast.
soil.verdict: MIXED — valley floor is fertile but small. Slopes are too steep for most farming.

microclimate.valleyFloor: Warmer, more humid. Rice and wheat possible.
microclimate.slopes: Steep, forested. Limited farming. Better for orchards.
microclimate.note: V-shaped valley creates dramatic microclimate differences over short distances.

mushroomEcology.verdict: EXCELLENT for wild — Parvati Valley has rich fungal diversity. Monsoon humidity ideal. Indoor lab possible.
mushroomEcology.wildSpecies: Rich diversity documented in Kullu district surveys.

pollinators.forageQuality: GOOD — alpine flowers, forest herbs, apple blossoms
pollinators.verdict: GOOD — shorter season than Kumaon due to steeper terrain.

mostCrops.notes: Steep V-valley = limited flat land. Only valley floor farming possible.

soil.type: Alluvial near Ganges, residual on hills
soil.fertility: Good near river, variable on hills
soil.verdict: GOOD near river. Variable on hills.

climate.note: Lower elevation (1200-3000ft) = warmer. Longer growing season. More subtropical crops possible.

microclimate.riverTerrace: Fertile, irrigated, warm. Best farming land.
microclimate.hillsides: Drier, thinner soil. Better for orchards.

mushroomEcology.verdict: GOOD — warmer than Kausani, more humidity from Ganges. But higher temps may favor different species.
